content.comment_body: Could someone assist me with [product_name] Web Editor? I'm struggling with using timers. For instance, I want timers to start each day at 8:00 and stop at 20:00. In the Web Editor, I created a table with Block Type: VW, access mode: Word. I can use analog value and block format: Unsigned, writable: yes. However, when connected to the webserver, I see the values displayed in a strange format. I want a block to enter 09:00 for start and 21:00 for stop, but the only setting available is VW with block format HEX. This shows values like 16#0900 instead of the regular time format. Thanks and sorry for my English.
Hi [user_name], welcome to the forum. I attached an example for you.

Thank you very much for the project and your assistance. My issue is that the value always appears as 16#2230, but I want it to show as 22:30. I've read a lot online about this, but I'm unsure if that's really correct?

Weekly timer switch times are saved in BCD format, with each time needing one word (2 bytes): hours in the left byte, minutes in the right. I separated these into bytes and displayed them as two analog values with a colon between. The web server can't display times in standard time format because they're stored as BCD codes, not usual time. The '16 #' prefix shows they're in HEX format. In my [product_name] Web Editor project, I managed to hide the '16 #' by making a modification.
What change did you make to block the display of '16 #'?
Hello, I believe it's in the JS folder, within the render file. Change the '#16' format at the end of the code.
Hi [user_name], welcome to the forum. Check out this topic: How to remove the hex marking (16#) when showing switch times for a weekly timer in the extended web server?
Hello, I can't download the example; clicking just refreshes the page without doing anything.
If you meant the example in post #2, it should download fine—no issues here.
Good morning! You can follow the steps shown in the attached photos. Book 1993. Regards.

Hello [user_name], welcome to the forum. This is an English-language forum, so please write your future posts in English. Thanks. Note that the topic started in May 2020, and at that time only [product_name] Web Editor V1.0.1 was available. That version did not have the feature shown in your screenshot. It was added in [product_name] Web Editor V1.1.

analysis.insight_summary: Users report confusion and dissatisfaction regarding how timer values are displayed in the web interface of [product_name] Web Editor. Instead of seeing times in standard (HH:MM) format, they see hexadecimal or BCD representations, which they find unintuitive. Attempts were made to modify these settings, but limitations within the native software's display remain, leading to requests for a more user-friendly solution.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want to enter and view timer values in the conventional time format (HH:MM) within the web interface, rather than seeing hexadecimal or BCD codes.
